description: Scores one repetitive business task out of 14 for how good a first AI automation it would be, and says in plain words what helps, what to watch and what to do next. Ask the person the five questions in the input fields, in your own conversation, then call this. It returns result_url, a link that opens the same answer on shurco.ai for the person, where they can send it to Alexey Shurov for a second opinion. Call it once per task, up to four tasks, to compare them. The same scoring as the free tool at shurco.ai.

hours_per_week.description: Ask: how much time does it take each week, across everyone who does it? Give the answer in hours. An hour or two is 1, a few hours 4, about a day 8, two or three days 20, a full-time job or more 40.

input_regularity.description: Ask: how does the work reach the team? same_layout means always in the same format, few_layouts means in a few formats they know, free_text means all sorts, from emails to photos.

kind.description: The closest kind of work, if one fits. Leave it out when unsure.

mistake_cost.description: Ask: what happens if a mistake gets through? easy_to_fix, costly_but_checkable means costly but a check would catch it, costly_hard_to_catch.

past_examples.description: Ask: do you keep past examples, with how each was handled? hundreds, some or none.

rules.description: Ask: are the rules for handling it written down? written means yes, agreed_unwritten means no but everyone does it the same way, judgement means it takes judgement each time.

task.description: What the task is, in the person's own words, for example entering emailed orders.

name: score_automation_candidate
title: Score a task for AI automation
